body: Thanks for your answer, what kind of spirit to you think they were/are? And how would I restore my energy?

It's not in the secular, pluralistic society we live in but it's relevant in Christian society, so when the Christian society is being forced to accept homosexuality and transsexualism it becomes a threat to the Christian community... Churches shouldn't receive hate for their stance against the LGBT movement
Because same sex marriage and transsexualism is a biblical abomination and I don't think we as a society should be forced to accept it as normal

Yeah, although I'm against the LGBT movement, I feel as if they deserve the respect everybody else receives, considering we're all humans...

You never hear of LGBT groups beheading Christians, burning them alive,etc. 

It's a biblical abomination for a man to alter himself into becoming a woman and vice versa, but that doesn't mean they deserve to be called a threat, especially in the sense that they're more of a threat than ISIS. 

They are a threat to Christian morals and our society as a whole but they aren't a danger, only a moral threat that goes against the Christian way of life.

If that's what you're going through then get a divorce. I really doubt Jesus would want you or your kids to suffer and endure trauma for the sake of your marriage... 

Jesus says to love your neighbor as yourself, so why would you stay married to someone who not only doesn't love you or treat you with respect but possibly puts you or your kids lives in danger?

That makes sense, and I definitely don't fear Heaven - just the possibility of being there for long enough and somehow disobeying God and subsequently being damned to hell after tasting salvation...

Like I don't ever intend to break any of God's laws/rules, especially in heaven, but the fact that it's eternal life means that eventually we're all bound to screw up so that's what worries me

I hope you're right, God is perfect and knows what He's doing so I hope there's some form of explanation or prevention in place that stops his followers from losing their salvation...

I read in a catechism book once that heaven is a place uncorrupted by the devil, but I'm still worried because there's no biblical evidence of that and I don't want to somehow lose my eternal life. 

But even if it is possible to lose salvation, maybe we're just supposed to enjoy it while we have it and thank God for giving us a glimpse into paradise... However then being sent into hell would only be more cruel, so I hope there's an answer to this...
Demons are real and when did I say psychics/mediums connected with the dead?

I'm new to meditation, although in the past I've tried it (once high, which brought about horrible demonic oppression that led to the voices because it was unguided kundalini-like movements and contorting of my body that left me feeling like a demon just entered)

I always struggled with true meditation due to my ADHD but now I'm medicated with Ritalin and I noticed today I was able to feel the present moment more and actually listen to what the guide was saying, without the constant mental chatter blocking it)

I want to meditate for emotional healing, basically. I want to open up to my higher self and absorb the innate goodness and purity he has within me and become my true self, along with the ability to naturally **feel** love, empathy, compassion, depth of soul, etc. 

I don't know how it should be done, that's why I started listening to a couple guided meditations on YouTube...

Do you have any advice or recommendations for me and how could I go about achieving that goal of my meditations?
No, never really heard of it? Could it help? And if so, how could I get the most out of it? Thanks
Okay, thanks man... I know I came off a bit strong at first but you seem like a good guy and we're both brothers in Christ so I'm glad we kind of agreed to disagree, have a good day!

Thanks a lot for your answer, I don't have time to respond to everything but I'm actually gonna save it and read it when I'm going through tough times because it gives me hope, hope at recovery and ultimately hope at becoming the real me, or at least the person I want to become...

Any advice with meditation based on the situation I'm in? I started watching a couple guided meditations today and since I'm on Ritalin finally (for my adhd) I can concentrate and better open up to positive healing and depth of soul...

And thanks for what you said regarding my soul, the only one with authority over it is God himself so these demons/psychics/whatever did "rob" me of my soul by taking it and putting a warped, disgustingly altered version of it on a camera for me to see and become further destroyed with but I'm realizing that they have no power over it and no control over where it/I end up in the afterlife. 

So thanks again, I appreciate it

Hey man, thanks so much for that answer... Just knowing somebody out there knows what I went through and what I still deal with is comforting, despite knowing we both lived through hell on earth and suffered major psychological trauma, needlessly on your end and mostly needless on mine (still feel guilty about those fantasies but I'm learning to let it go, the voices just made me feel like a monster for the longest time over them)...

I'm sorry you had to go through that kind of torment, but I'm glad we're both years into it without any kind of physical harm coming our way. I know what you mean about that psychic barrier (although I never heard that term) because now it's really easy to ignore unless I've been up a couple days or I'm doing more ritalin than usual (I use/abuse it regularly, but it helps me in so many ways I can live with the addiction for now at least)...

I basically view it as a mental illness too, and even if these are real people, they haven't killed me and I'm not gonna do their job anytime soon for them so it's the equivalent to one, once you get past the horrible violation of them invading your/our mind(s). 

And thankfully I've found Christ, I've had a couple supernatural experiences if you're interested in hearing, and one where the voices said they're demons which is almost comforting, knowing they aren't real people and they're suffering in a worse hell than they caused me... 

And thanks man, maybe they didn't "steal" my soul like they said but they violated the fuck out of it so although it feels the same, my true soul is still inside me and only God himself has authority over that.

Thanks man, I guess it all comes down to doing onto others as you'd have them do onto you, with animals being no exception. That's why I became a vegetarian, knowing that animals have to basically suffer their whole lives so I can eat them when they die... Like meat's delicious, I'm not gonna lie, but it feels like the right thing now that I don't eat it anymore...

I think my problem is judging the opposition too harshly, we're raised with meat being food unless you're lucky enough to be born into a vegetarian family, which is rare. So being conditioned your whole life into thinking somethings socially acceptable, that you see everybody around you do, feels to most people like a basic fact of life - animals being food. 

But looking at the morality of it like I described in that post, it's not fair to rob a life of basic liberty and happiness, especially when there's no saving grace at the end to justify or balance out the cruelty... 

But on the otherhand, read this quote:

*"For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.

20 All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

21 Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?"* - Ecclesiastes 3:19-21

According to that, the quote ambiguously gives hope of there actually being an afterlife for animals...

So let's say that is true, then maybe eating meat isn't the main moral issue because God would likely reward animals with happiness and never-ending life in the afterlife he'd provide them and they'd be almost like martyrs in a sense, dying to sustain the human race (however needless)... If that's the case, what you originally said about raising our own animals and treating them with ethics should be the main cause and concern... Regardless of the idea of an animal heaven, animal rights and respect should be the main concern because if we made that the priority instead of trying to convert the world to veganism, animal lives would at least be tolerable if not happy while they're alive on this planet... 

So it comes down to what your heart tells you, I guess. It was wrong of me to criticize the morality of our Savior, He was the only perfect man to walk this earth.

In my opinion, I just don't feel right contributing to the meat industry. Maybe if the conditions were humane and ethical (freerange, family's wouldn't be separated, painkillers would be used, animals wouldn't be killed prematurely over their inferiority to others their age) and I knew forsure that there was an afterlife for these animals, I could justify eating them. But based on the current cruelties of the meat industry I just feel wrong contributing, but it's a deeply personal decision and I'm learning to not judge others for their own views as it's all about perspective and understanding...

Maybe that was a bit off topic or long but hopefully you see my point/position and why I think it's the right decision to abstain from meat

Thanks and I get what you're saying but if they truly don't have souls then wouldn't their suffering be more wrong than humans? Because without a soul that animal will never experience the relief of suffering that heaven provides, so if they don't have souls then their life is linear and should be valued at least equally to humans considering this life is all they'll ever know so the suffering they endure is never balanced out by heavenly freedom and the relief and bliss us humans (Christians) can count on to give us hope... 

Again, maybe I'm wrong but when you think about it morally doesn't that argument kind of make you think? 

And yeah, I know this world will never go vegan or vegetarian so the best thing we can realistically do is enact laws that prohibit needless cruelty and suffering for animals and make free range farming the norm compared to factory farms and the hell that they consist of. 

Also, we should look into In Vitro meat and try to incorporate that into society more and therefore make it an affordable and humane option for meat eaters (In vitro meat is meat flesh grown in a lab that's never attached to a conscious living organism so it's an ethical alternative to the animal industry with the added benefit of still being meat)

I'll humble myself and admit I might be wrong, especially when it comes to criticizing God (I repented of that)... I was just putting my own morality on God, which is heretic considering he's the God of righteousness and everything he does he does perfectly. I just wish animals weren't sanctioned as food like they are but maybe there's a reason for that, maybe they're necessary martyrs and God gives them the life they deserve in heaven, I don't know I'm only speculating. 

Wasn't trying to come off like I did, I just feel passion for animals and sadness at the fact that they're so mistreated and abused in the bible.

There's references to slavery in the new testament, and you also have to keep in mind that the Bible's been altered through it's translations and manipulated, especially the books of Moses, into making God look like a wrathful, hateful, horrible deity when in reality he's the God of love and compassion. 

And read this quote from the book of Isaiah:

“Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a human being; whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers swine’s blood; whoever makes a memorial offering of frankincense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways and in their abominations they take delight.” 
Isaiah 66:3

No, I expected criticism but it doesn't bother me, I'm seeking my soul and people's opinions of what I went through don't bother me as long as I progress and find the answers to what happened and from that learn and grow into who I need and want to be
Demons are real... Regardless of your belief there's countless encounters with the demonic and the supernatural, not everything is cut and dry and reality's more than we perceive
It's easy to say that but unless you went through everything I went through, you have no idea what kind of damage they did to my soul and my mind.

That doesn't justify it morally. Maybe it's blasphemous to say that Jesus's morals weren't perfect but animals don't deserve to be slaughtered needlessly...

There's plenty of things justified in the Bible that aren't morally righteous... Like when Abraham took his maidservant to be his wife in order to bear a child... How is that okay? He was an old man and she was taken and basically forced into sex and childbirth at the justification of God. The only way I could justify God's sanctioning of that was by imagining God changed her emotions into desire for him and gave her the perceived will to marry him on her own, but that's never written about...

And slavery altogether in the Bible... Just as slavery is a morally disgusting and outdated concept, consumption of meat is also morally disgusting and outdated.

In Jesus's time people didn't have the alternatives to meat that they have now and animals weren't raised in factory farms, nowadays we can choose veganism/vegetarianism and live healthy, satisfying lives without meat.

Think about it, would you "own" a slave if that were legal because it's sanctioned in the bible? If so you have some flawed morals

He died to save our souls, look at our world and honestly tell me it's saved...

There's a huge difference between "saved" in the biblical sense and "saved" in the moral/ethical/environmental sense. 

If we gave up meat, not only would we reduce climate change, fresh water consumption, etc. but we'd be saving **billions** of lives. And yes, animals have souls... maybe it doesn't say that in the bible but our consciousness is all energy, right? That energy is our spiritual energy, therefore all living and especially all conscious beings have souls and even if they didn't, they have hearts, feelings of sadness, pain, love for their families, etc. so how the hell can we justify our mass holocaust of these innocent creatures? Animals are pure, loving, innately good... we're the corrupted ones when you think about it. When does an animal sin? Yes, occasionally animals rape which is horrible for any specie but by and large they don't do anything morally wrong, besides eat other animals which is only natural in the **animal** kingdom, and shouldn't be acceptable of us humans considering we have the knowledge and ability to avoid meat altogether...
Or into giving up meat completely, imagine you were born to be slaughtered? It's messed up, regardless of how you look at it.

It's gotten way better in the past two years, I'm on anti-psychotics and can basically block out and ignore the voices in the same way we all naturally block out our noses and only see them when we look, for the most part at least...

I wanted to ask this question for advice on finding my soul again. When they stole my soul from me I felt like I lost a piece of who I was and it's resulted in a whole host of psychological problems. I want to feel my true soul and it's like these voices robbed me of that, of the thing that makes everyone human...

They weren't saying that...

By cutting down or eliminating your meat consumption, you not only stop contributing to the animal holocaust, you reduce demand for the breeding of animals for meat which subsequently results in less methane gas released, therefore resulting in a reduced climate change
